records.reportedResult: 282 randomized; 24-week peak oxygen uptake least-squares mean placebo-adjusted difference +1.7 mL/kg/min; 95% CI +1.0 to +2.4; P<0.001.
records.referenceContext: Later anchor-based clinical-importance analysis includes SEQUOIA-HCM and MAPLE-HCM, but a patient-level minimal important change cannot be treated as a calibrated RAAS benchmark or historical forecast.
records.reviewNeeded: Recheck endpoint prespecification and SAP, estimate clinical relevance, inspect missing data, subgroup interactions and safety; lock an independent comparator before any provisional grade.

records.sourceTitle: SEQUOIA-HCM KCCQ and health status results
records.reportedResult: 282 randomized; at 24 weeks placebo-adjusted KCCQ-OSS mean difference +7.9 points, 95% CI +4.8 to +11.0, P<0.001; 29.7% on aficamten versus 12.4% placebo had >=20-point improvement.
records.referenceContext: An independent patient-level meta-analysis notes group-mean KCCQ differences and individual minimal-important-change thresholds require care; do not infer individual response from group means alone.
records.reviewNeeded: Verify analysis population and missing PRO data, the clinical meaning of the group effect and trial-specific KCCQ interpretation. No automatic grade based on a single threshold.

records.sourceTitle: MAPLE-HCM randomized aficamten versus metoprolol Phase 3 results
records.reportedResult: 175 randomized; 24-week peak oxygen uptake between-group difference +2.3 mL/kg/min (95% CI +1.5 to +3.1), P<0.001, versus metoprolol.
records.referenceContext: SEQUOIA-HCM is a separate placebo-controlled trial of the same therapy and obstructive HCM but is not a head-to-head comparison of the MAPLE active control or a calibrated effect-size cutoff.
records.reviewNeeded: Reconcile MAPLE protocol, active comparator, missing data, multiplicity and safety; avoid pooling placebo and metoprolol controls as equivalent.
